brief: GS's weekly US flows note ties a softer-than-expected September payrolls print (+29k vs ~90k consensus, two-month revisions of -60k, unemployment to 4.2%) and a cooler core PCE (+0.2% m/m, 3.0% y/y) to October FOMC hike odds falling from 64% to under 25%. GS Economics pulls its next hike from October to December and flags a meaningful chance no further hikes are needed, while Q2 GDP was revised up to +2.2% and Q3 tracking sits at +3.3%. On energy, a G7/IEA release of up to 100m barrels of diesel and crude follows two tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz and an Iranian warning the strait stays closed, framed as supporting disinflation. S&P 500 market breadth has fallen to its weakest since the Dot Com era (median stock 17% below its high versus the index 2% from its ATH) even as positioning stays light (Sentiment Indicator -0.7 SD, hedge funds de-risking, three straight weeks of single-stock shorting), so Esposito and EU trading's Privorotsky both call the pain trade an upside bleed, though Privorotsky flags France and Eastern Europe risk. Q3 S&P EPS growth of 27% is forecast to lean heavily on AI infrastructure, Tech and Energy; GIR adds AMZN, BURL, HII, JCI and OXY to its Conviction List, and Mehta upgrades OXY to Buy while downgrading TOU to Sell.
